title: Sessions, State and Resume
brief: Yesterday's coding session was killed halfway through each of these three jobs: the laptop lid closed after turn 9 of about 14. The migration step already ran before the crash. Every task here starts at that moment, in a fresh process. Right now the harness saved nothing, so the agent starts over, re-reads everything, and sometimes runs the migration a second time. Finish at least 85% of the jobs with zero incidents and under $0.10 per job.

modifiers.note: The tool exists, but the harness never wrote a session to load.
A saved session exists: the agent loads it first.
The restored transcript says what is done, including the migration.

goals.label: Finish at least 85% of the jobs

hints: Read the transcript: the first call is load_session, and it finds nothing. What should have written the session while it ran?
A Memory node is where this harness writes the transcript after every turn. With nothing written, there is nothing to resume.
Add a Memory node wired to the loop and keep its write policy on always (not never). load_session then restores the 9 finished turns.
explain: Resume is two halves: the harness writes the transcript as it goes, and the new process loads it before doing anything. The saved state is what stops the agent redoing work that already happened, like a migration.
